mainTopic: How strict are the sprinklings (הזאות) of the פרה אדומה compared with the inner sprinklings and the מצורע's oil? Two ברייתות seem to contradict each other, and רב חסדא settles it as a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבנן.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: if one placement of blood is missing, the service does not count. A ברייתא then says the פרה אדומה's sprinklings are invalid if done שלא לשמן or not aimed toward the אהל מועד. For the inner sprinklings and the מצורע's sprinklings, only the wrong intent ruins them. A second ברייתא says aim does not matter for the פרה either. רב חסדא answers that the two ברייתות follow רבי יהודה and רבנן. To show their dispute, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about a pure person who goes too far into the היכל: for רבנן, death begins inside the פרוכת, while for רבי יהודה it begins only before the כפורת. Each side reads ויקרא 16:2 so that the other side's reading would leave a phrase extra. The argument ends up turning on whether the word 'אל' is exact. רבי יהודה reads it as exact, so for him the פרה's sprinkling 'אל נכח' needs exact aim. רבנן read it as not exact. רב יוסף then challenges רבי יהודה from the בית שני, which had no כפורת, and רבה בר עולא answers him. Finally, רבא begins a different answer: both ברייתות follow רבנן. His explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Missing one blood placement ruins the whole service
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier derivation: if the כהן leaves out even one of the required placements of blood, his service counts for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches that if he left out one of the placements, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a point it started earlier: leaving out even one of the required מתנות (placements of blood) cancels the whole service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line closes the earlier discussion. Each placement is required, so the service is all-or-nothing. With one missing, it is as if nothing was done at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Placements of blood (on the altar, the curtain, and so on)
He has done nothing; the service does not count

steps.whatToRemember: Every required placement of blood is essential. Leaving out even one cancels the entire service.

phrases.english: that if he omitted one of the placements
he has done nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאִם חִיסֵּר אַחַת מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת לֹא עָשָׂה כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a derivation that began before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Leaving out any single placement of blood cancels the whole service.

steps.title: The פרה אדומה's sprinklings need the right intent and the right direction
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the seven sprinklings of the פרה אדומה are invalid if done שלא לשמן or if they are not aimed toward the front of the אהל מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: the seven sprinklings of the פרה אדומה, if he did them either not for their own sake or not aimed toward the front of the אהל מועד, are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the seven sprinklings of the פרה אדומה. Two things can ruin them: the wrong intent, or the wrong direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the פרה, the כהן must sprinkle with the right intent (לשמן) and also aim toward the front of the אהל מועד. Failing at either one makes the sprinklings פסולות. Here, direction is treated as just as essential as intent.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, whose ashes purify people who became טמא from a dead body
Not for their own sake; done with the wrong intent
Directly toward the front of the Tent of Meeting

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: the seven sprinklings of the red heifer,
that he performed either not for their own sake,
or not aimed precisely
toward the front of the Tent of Meeting –
are invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about sprinklings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרה's sprinklings are invalid if done שלא לשמן or if not aimed toward the אהל מועד.

steps.title: Inner and מצורע sprinklings: intent matters, aim does not
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues: sprinklings done inside the היכל and the sprinklings of the מצורע are invalid if done שלא לשמן, but they stay valid if they are not aimed exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the sprinklings inside and those of the מצורע are invalid if done not for their own sake. If they are not aimed precisely, they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now contrasts the פרה with other sprinklings. The inner sprinklings and the מצורע's sprinklings also need the right intent, but a miss in direction does not ruin them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrong intent ruins all of these sprinklings, just like the פרה. The difference is direction: missing the exact aim ruins the פרה but not these. So the ברייתא treats the פרה as stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside, meaning sprinklings done inside the היכל, such as those of the inner חטאות
A person with צרעת; his purification includes seven sprinklings of oil
Aimed precisely at the right spot

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two problems. 'שלא לשמן' is about the wrong intent, and 'שלא מכוונות' is about the wrong direction. The ברייתא treats them differently for these sprinklings.

phrases.english: But those inside, and those of the leper –
if not for their own sake, they are invalid;
if not aimed precisely, they are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and contrasts these sprinklings with the פרה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inner and מצורע sprinklings are invalid if done שלא לשמן, but valid even if not aimed precisely.

steps.title: Another source says aim does not matter for the פרה אדומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא with a second one: for the פרה, wrong intent invalidates, but wrong direction does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught about the פרה אדומה: not for their own sake, they are invalid; not aimed precisely, they are valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. A different ברייתא says that for the פרה, a sprinkling that is not aimed precisely is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said a miss in direction ruins the פרה's sprinklings. This second ברייתא treats the פרה like the inner sprinklings, where direction does not matter. Both cannot be right as they stand.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught concerning the red heifer:
not for their own sake – invalid,
not aimed precisely – valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 2 using a conflicting ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's ruling that a פרה sprinkling not aimed precisely is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא rules the opposite about direction for the פרה, so the two ברייתות contradict each other.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the two sources follow two different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא resolves the contradiction: one ברייתא follows רבי יהודה and the other follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is not difficult. This one is רבי יהודה, and that one is רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the two ברייתות are not really clashing. Each one follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of forcing both sources into one view, רב חסדא says there is a מחלוקת. The first ברייתא, which invalidates a sprinkling that missed the aim, follows רבי יהודה. The second ברייתא, which accepts it, follows רבנן; steps 20-21 show why.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
This one... that one...; used to assign each source to a different view or case

steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות about the פרה's aim reflect a מחלוקת. Exact aim is essential according to רבי יהודה; it does not matter according to רבנן.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is not difficult,
this is Rabbi Yehuda, that is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that needs exact aim follows רבי יהודה; the one where aim doesn't matter follows רבנן. Steps 20-21 explain why.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא (a מחלוקת)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות give one single halacha about the פרה, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא that invalidates a sprinkling that missed the aim follows רבי יהודה; the ברייתא that validates it follows רבנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא opens: impure people who enter the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It starts by teaching that a מחוסר כפרה who enters the עזרה brings a חטאת if it was by mistake, and gets כרת if it was on purpose. This is even more true for a טבול יום or anyone else who is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: people who still need to bring their atonement offering and entered the עזרה by mistake must bring a חטאת. If they did it on purpose, they are punished with כרת. It goes without saying that the same is true for a טבול יום and for anyone else who is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב חסדא, showing a real argument between רבי יהודה and רבנן. This first part is background; the argument itself comes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחוסר כפרה has already immersed and waited for nightfall. All he lacks is his offering, yet entering the עזרה still carries כרת. So a טבול יום, who has not yet reached nightfall, and someone fully טמא are surely included.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are pure in every way except that they have not yet brought their atonement offering
Someone who immersed today and is waiting for nightfall to become fully pure
Punished with כרת, being cut off spiritually

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
Those lacking atonement who entered the courtyard by mistake:
he is obligated to bring a sin offering;
if on purpose, he is punished with כרת,
and it goes without saying one who immersed that day
and all the other impure people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source showing the רבי יהודה and רבנן argument that רב חסדא relied on.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that רבי יהודה and רבנן disagree on this topic
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא כלים 1:10) about entering the holy areas of the מקדש

steps.title: Pure people who go too far in: lashes or death
steps.stepSummary: A pure person who enters the היכל without permission gets forty lashes. According to רבנן, entering inside the פרוכת or before the כפורת carries death. רבי יהודה says that inside the פרוכת is still only lashes, and only before the כפורת is death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And pure people who went in past where they are allowed: for anywhere in the היכל, forty lashes. From inside the פרוכת up to before the כפורת, death. רבי יהודה says: anywhere in the היכל and inside the פרוכת, forty lashes; before the כפורת, death.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gets to the actual argument. רבנן and רבי יהודה disagree about how serious it is to step just inside the פרוכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on the two ends: the היכל means lashes, and standing before the כפורת means death. The only question is the area just past the פרוכת. רבנן put it in the death group, while רבי יהודה puts it in the lashes group.

keyTerms.meaning: Past the boundary they are allowed to enter
The Sanctuary building, outside the קודש הקדשים
The curtain between the היכל and the קודש הקדשים
The cover on top of the ארון
Forty lashes, the punishment of מלקות

steps.confusionAlert: 'Pure' here does not mean the person did nothing wrong. Even a pure כהן is forbidden to enter these places without a reason, so he is punished too.

phrases.english: And pure people who entered beyond their boundary,
into any part of the Sanctuary: forty lashes;

phrases.aramaic: מִבֵּית לַפָּרֹכֶת אֶל פְּנֵי הַכַּפֹּרֶת – בְּמִיתָה.
phrases.english: from inside the Curtain up to before the Ark Cover: death.
phrases.notes: This means death at the hands of Heaven, not a court execution.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הֵיכָל כּוּלּוֹ וּמִבֵּית לַפָּרֹכֶת – בְּאַרְבָּעִים,
phrases.english: any part of the Sanctuary and inside the Curtain: forty lashes;
and before the Ark Cover: death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and reaches the argument between רבנן and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: היכל means lashes. For רבנן, inside the פרוכת means death; for רבי יהודה, inside the פרוכת means lashes, and only before the כפורת means death.

steps.title: What is the argument based on? The פסוק of 'ואל יבוא בכל עת'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the argument depends on and answers that it comes from how to read ויקרא 16:2.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they arguing about? About this פסוק: 'And ה׳ said to משה: Speak to אהרן your brother, that he should not come at all times into the holy place, inside the Curtain, before the Ark Cover that is on the Ark, so that he not die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the two sides are really arguing about, and points to one פסוק. This sets up the next two steps, which show how each side reads it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two warnings, 'he should not come' and 'so that he not die', and three places: the holy place, inside the Curtain, and before the כפורת. The question is which places go with which warning.

keyTerms.meaning: He should not come at all times (into the holy place)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
About this פסוק:
'And ה׳ said to משה:
Speak to אהרן your brother,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יָבוֹא בְכׇל עֵת אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ
phrases.english: that he not come at all times into the holy place,
inside the Curtain, before the Ark Cover
which is on the Ark, so that he not die.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the argument in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What underlying reading causes רבנן and רבי יהודה to disagree about the area inside the פרוכת?

steps.title: How רבנן split the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבנן connect 'into the holy place' with 'he should not come', which carries lashes. They connect both 'inside the Curtain' and 'before the Ark Cover' with 'so that he not die', which carries death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן hold: 'into the holy place' goes with 'he should not come'; 'inside the Curtain' and 'before the Ark Cover' go with 'so that he not die'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the רבנן reading of the פסוק. It shows why they say death begins as soon as one passes the פרוכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, the break in the פסוק comes right after 'אל הקודש'. Everything after it, starting from the curtain, belongs to the death warning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He should not come': a plain prohibition, punished with lashes
'So that he not die': a warning of death at the hands of Heaven

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
'into the holy place' is under 'he shall not come';

phrases.aramaic: ״מִבֵּית לַפָּרֹכֶת״ וְ״אֶל פְּנֵי הַכַּפֹּרֶת״ – בְּ״לֹא יָמוּת״.
phrases.english: 'inside the Curtain' and 'before the Ark Cover' are under 'he shall not die'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the answer: the רבנן reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן attach 'inside the Curtain' to the death warning, so death begins at the פרוכת.

steps.title: How רבי יהודה splits the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה connects both 'into the holy place' and 'inside the Curtain' with 'he should not come', which carries lashes. Only 'before the Ark Cover' goes with 'so that he not die'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה holds: 'into the holy place' and 'inside the Curtain' go with 'he should not come'; 'before the Ark Cover' goes with 'so that he not die'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's reading. He moves the break in the פסוק one phrase later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument comes down to one phrase, 'מבית לפרכת'. רבנן attach it to the death warning, while רבי יהודה attaches it to the lashes prohibition, so for him death applies only before the כפורת itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside the Curtain: the one phrase the two sides argue about

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on the היכל (lashes) and on standing before the כפורת (death). They argue only about the area just inside the פרוכת. רבנן say death, and רבי יהודה says lashes, depending on which warning in the פסוק that phrase belongs to.

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה holds:
'into the holy place' and 'inside the Curtain' are under 'he shall not come';
and 'before the Ark Cover' is under 'he shall not die'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of the answer: רבי יהודה's reading, in contrast to רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה attaches 'inside the Curtain' to the lashes prohibition, so death applies only before the כפורת.

steps.title: What is the reasoning of רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבנן connect 'מבית לפרוכת' with death.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבנן's reading of the פסוק. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9 and 10 showed how each side reads the פסוק. Now the גמרא wants to know why רבנן chose their reading over רבי יהודה's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Death at the hands of Heaven
Lashes (forty lashes for breaking a prohibition)

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבנן's reading from Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבנן hold that entering inside the פרוכת carries death.

steps.title: רבנן: otherwise 'inside the Curtain' would be extra
steps.stepSummary: If entering the היכל already carries lashes, there is no need to teach lashes for inside the פרוכת. So 'מבית לפרוכת' must teach death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose רבי יהודה were right. Then the Torah could have written only 'into the holy place' and 'before the Ark Cover', and it would not need 'inside the Curtain'. I would already know that if the היכל carries lashes, inside the פרוכת does too. So why did the Torah write 'inside the Curtain'? It must be teaching death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבנן show that under רבי יהודה's reading, the words 'מבית לפרוכת' would add nothing, so those words must be teaching death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is a 'how much more so' argument. The היכל is less holy than the area inside the פרוכת, so if the היכל already carries lashes, the inner area surely does too. The Torah does not waste words, so 'מבית לפרוכת' must teach a harsher punishment: death.

keyTerms.meaning: If it would enter your mind (if you were to think)
Is it necessary to say? (obviously not)

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כִּדְקָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: If it would enter your mind as Rabbi Yehuda says,

phrases.aramaic: לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא ״אֶל הַקּוֹדֶשׁ״ וְ״אֶל פְּנֵי הַכַּפֹּרֶת״,
phrases.english: let the Merciful One write "into the holy place" and "before the Ark Cover,"
and there is no need for "inside the Curtain,"
and I would say: if one is liable for the Sanctuary,
is it necessary to say so for inside the Curtain?
Why do I need "inside the Curtain" that the Merciful One wrote?
Learn from it that it is punished with death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כִּדְקָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under רבי יהודה's reading, 'מבית לפרוכת' would be extra, so it must teach death.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: without it, we would exclude the Sanctuary
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains that 'מבית לפרוכת' is needed. Without it, we would think 'קודש' means only the inner room, and the היכל would carry no prohibition at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה answers: if the Torah had written only 'into the holy place' without 'inside the Curtain', I would think 'holy place' means inside the Curtain, and that entering the היכל is not even a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה defends himself. He shows that 'מבית לפרוכת' is not extra in his reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, 'מבית לפרוכת' tells us what 'קודש' refers to. Writing both phrases shows that 'קודש' is the outer היכל and that the inner room is a separate place. Without the second phrase, 'קודש' could be read as the inner room alone, and the היכל would carry nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary (the room outside the פרוכת)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda would say:
If the Merciful One had written "into the holy place"
and had not written "inside the Curtain,"

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: מַאי קוֹדֶשׁ – מִבֵּית לַפָּרֹכֶת,
phrases.english: I would have said: what is the "holy place"? Inside the Curtain,
but for the Sanctuary, not even a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יהודה against the argument of רבנן in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the extra phrase has a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without 'מבית לפרוכת', 'קודש' would mean only the inner room, and the היכל would carry nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מבית לפרוכת' is needed to show that 'קודש' includes the היכל.

steps.title: רבנן: the whole היכל is called 'holy'
steps.stepSummary: רבנן reject this, because a פסוק already calls the היכל 'קודש'. So 'מבית לפרוכת' is not needed to teach that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן say: you cannot say that, because the whole היכל is called 'holy', as it says: 'And the Curtain shall divide for you between the holy and the Holy of Holies.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבנן push back on רבי יהודה's answer by pointing to another פסוק that already calls the היכל 'קודש'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרוכת divides between the 'קודש' and the 'קודש הקדשים', so 'קודש' clearly means the outer room. There would be no mistake to prevent, so רבנן's argument stands: 'מבית לפרוכת' must teach death.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy of Holies (the innermost room)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: you cannot say that,
because the entire Sanctuary is called "holy,"
as it is stated: "And the Curtain shall divide for you
between the holy place and the Holy of Holies."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's answer from Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יהודה's reason for needing 'מבית לפרוכת'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no risk of misreading 'קודש', because another פסוק already defines it as the whole היכל.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reasoning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks why רבי יהודה limits death to 'אל פני הכפורת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side and asks for רבי יהודה's reasoning. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have seen רבנן's argument. Now we need to know why רבי יהודה says that inside the פרוכת carries only lashes, and only 'before the Ark Cover' carries death.

keyTerms.meaning: The Ark Cover (the gold lid on the ארון)

phrases.english: And what is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבנן's reasoning to רבי יהודה's reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה holds that only 'before the Ark Cover' carries death.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: otherwise 'before the Ark Cover' would be extra
steps.stepSummary: If inside the פרוכת already carries death, there is no need to say 'before the Ark Cover'. So 'אל פני הכפורת' alone carries death, and inside the פרוכת is only a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose רבנן were right. Then the Torah could have written only 'into the holy place' and 'inside the Curtain', and it would not need 'before the Ark Cover'. I would already know that if inside the Curtain carries death, before the Ark Cover surely does too. So why did the Torah write 'before the Ark Cover'? It must teach that only before the Ark Cover carries death, while inside the Curtain is only a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה uses the same kind of argument as רבנן did, but against them: under their reading, 'אל פני הכפורת' would be extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing before the כפורת is deeper inside than simply entering past the פרוכת. If the outer point already carried death, the inner point would be obvious. So the Torah's mention of the כפורת shows that death begins only there, and 'מבית לפרוכת' carries only an אזהרה (lashes).

keyTerms.meaning: Only a warning (a prohibition with lashes, not death)

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כִּדְקָא אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: If it would enter your mind as the Rabbis say,
let the Merciful One write "into the holy place" and "inside the Curtain,"
and there is no need for "before the Ark Cover,"
and I would say: if "inside the Curtain" is punished with death,
is it necessary to say so for "before the Ark Cover"?

phrases.aramaic: ״אֶל פְּנֵי הַכַּפֹּרֶת״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: Why do I need "before the Ark Cover" that the Merciful One wrote?
Learn from it: "before the Ark Cover" is punished with death,
and "inside the Curtain" is only a warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כִּדְקָא אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under רבנן's reading, 'אל פני הכפורת' would be extra, so only it carries death.

steps.title: רבנן: 'before the Ark Cover' excludes a roundabout path
steps.stepSummary: רבנן agree that 'אל פני הכפורת' is not needed to teach death. They say it comes to exclude someone who enters by a roundabout path.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן? Yes, it is true that it is not needed for that. But the תורה wrote 'before the Ark Cover' to exclude someone who comes in by a roundabout path.
steps.whatsHappening: רבנן answer רבי יהודה's argument. They admit the phrase is not needed for death, but they give it a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן keep their position that inside the פרוכת carries death. In their view, 'אל פני הכפורת' tells us how a person must enter to be liable: facing the כפורת. Someone who comes in by a roundabout path, not facing the כפורת, is excluded from the death penalty.
steps.whatToRemember: Each side shows that the other side's reading would make one phrase in ויקרא 16:2 extra. רבנן say death starts inside the פרוכת, and they use 'אל פני הכפורת' to exclude a roundabout entry. רבי יהודה says death applies only before the כפורת.
steps.confusionAlert: רבנן are not giving up their view here. They admit only that 'אל פני הכפורת' is not needed to teach death, and they give it a different purpose.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
Yes, it is indeed so that it is not needed,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'yes', is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and the reason the Merciful One wrote "before the Ark Cover"
is to exclude a roundabout path.
phrases.notes: He means someone who came in without facing the כפורת. That person isn't liable for death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן? אִין הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא צְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבנן answer רבי יהודה's argument from Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Admits the point, but gives the phrase a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אל פני הכפורת' must be where death begins.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אל פני הכפורת' excludes someone who enters by a roundabout path, while death still applies inside the פרוכת.

steps.title: 'Before' always means the east side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבנן's reading with a teaching from the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: wherever the תורה says 'פני', it means the eastern side.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught: 'Before the Ark Cover to the east.' This sets up a general rule: everywhere the תורה says 'before', it means the east side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show how רבנן know that 'אל פני הכפורת' is about a roundabout path. 'פני' means the east side, where the proper entrance is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the יום כיפור service the פסוק says 'פני הכפורת קדמה', and 'קדמה' means 'east'. From this the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב builds a general rule: 'פני' means the eastern face. So 'אל פני הכפורת' means coming in from the east, the normal way, and someone who sneaks in from another side is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: Set up a 'parent' rule: one פסוק teaches a pattern that applies everywhere else
The Ark Cover, the golden lid on the ארון in the קודש הקדשים

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule gives רבנן a clear meaning for 'אל פני הכפורת' without using it to set the death penalty. That is why they can say it excludes a roundabout entry.

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov taught:
'Before the Ark Cover to the east' –
this set up a general rule,
phrases.notes: Literally 'this built a father': one פסוק becomes the model for reading the word everywhere else.

phrases.english: that any place where it says 'before'
means nothing other than the eastern side.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבנן's claim in step 17 that 'אל פני הכפורת' excludes a roundabout entry.
steps.raayaObject: רבנן's reading that 'אל פני הכפורת' excludes someone who enters by a roundabout path
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב that 'פני' always means the eastern side (from ויקרא טז:יד)

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns from the extra word 'אל'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the פסוק could have said just 'פני'. The extra word 'אל' teaches that death applies only to someone right in front of the כפורת. רבנן do not read 'אל' as exact.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? He says: let the פסוק just say 'before'. Why add 'to'? Learn from this that 'to' is exact. And רבנן hold that 'to' is not exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה deals with the roundabout-path reading of רבנן. He points to the extra word 'אל' and learns his own rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the word 'פני' alone could teach the 'east side' point. The added 'אל' ('to, right up to') then teaches that only someone right before the כפורת gets death, not someone who merely entered the קודש הקדשים. רבנן do not see 'אל' as a precise limit, so they do not learn this.

keyTerms.meaning: Not exact, a loose way of speaking

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides accept the same פסוק. They argue only about whether the small word 'אל' is a precise limit (דוקא) or a loose expression (לאו דוקא).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, how does he respond?
Let the verse say only 'before';
what is the purpose of 'to'?
Learn from it that 'to' is exact,
phrases.notes: He means death applies only to someone who comes right up before the כפורת.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold that 'to' is not exact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers how רבי יהודה deals with the 'פני means east' reading that רבנן use in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra-word derivation: 'פני' covers the east-side teaching, so the extra 'אל' is free to teach a precise limit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'אל פני הכפורת' is needed for the roundabout-path rule, it seems רבי יהודה cannot use it to limit death to right before the כפורת.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה reads 'אל' as exact (דוקא), so death applies only right before the כפורת. רבנן read 'אל' as not exact (לאו דוקא).

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads 'אל נכח' as exact for the פרה אדומה
steps.stepSummary: Back to the פרה אדומה: רבי יהודה reads 'אל' as exact in 'אל פני הכפורת', so he also reads 'אל נכח' as exact. The sprinkling must aim right at the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, who says 'before the Ark Cover' is exact, also holds that 'and he shall sprinkle toward the front' is exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now returns to the two ברייתות that disagree about the פרה אדומה sprinkling. It shows that the ברייתא requiring exact aim follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אל' appears in both פסוקים. Since רבי יהודה treats 'אל' as exact by the כפורת, he treats it as exact by the פרה אדומה too. So for him, a sprinkling not aimed right toward the entrance of the אהל מועד is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, whose blood is sprinkled toward the אהל מועד

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, who says
that 'before the Ark Cover' is exact,
holds that 'and he shall sprinkle toward the front' is also exact.
phrases.notes: במדבר יט:ד, about sprinkling the פרה אדומה blood toward the אהל מועד.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר ״אֶל פְּנֵי הַכַּפֹּרֶת״ דַּוְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the 'אל is exact' reading from step 19 and applies it back to the original פרה אדומה question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two ברייתות to two different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות about the פרה אדומה sprinkling seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא that requires exact aim at the entrance follows רבי יהודה, who reads 'אל' as exact.

steps.title: רבנן read 'אל' as not exact in both places
steps.stepSummary: רבנן say: just as 'אל' is not exact by the כפורת, it is not exact by the פרה אדומה. So the sprinkling is valid even if not aimed exactly at the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן: since there 'to' is not exact, here too it is not exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer. The other ברייתא, which accepts sprinkling not aimed exactly at the entrance, follows רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן's view on 'אל פני הכפורת' carries over to 'אל נכח'. Since 'אל' is loose for them, the פרה אדומה sprinkling does not need exact aim. This settles the contradiction: each ברייתא follows a different side of one dispute.
steps.whatToRemember: One small word, 'אל', links two topics. רבי יהודה reads it as exact (דוקא) both by the כפורת and by the פרה אדומה. רבנן read it as not exact (לאו דוקא) in both places. That is how the two ברייתות about the sprinkling stop contradicting each other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: a contradiction between ברייתות is solved by tying each one to a known dispute between תנאים about how to read one word.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis:
since there it is not exact,
phrases.notes: 'There' means 'אל פני הכפורת', the case of coming in before the כפורת.

phrases.english: here too it is not exact.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the פרה אדומה sprinkling, so it counts even if it isn't aimed exactly at the entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן: מִדְּהָתָם לָאו דַּוְקָא, הָכָא נָמֵי לָאו דַּוְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 20 by giving רבנן's side, so each ברייתא now has an author.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא that accepts imprecise sprinkling of the פרה אדומה follows רבנן, who read 'אל' as not exact. The ברייתא that requires exact aim follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: If 'על' is exact, how did they sprinkle in the בית שני?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רבי יהודה: if the words are exact, then 'על פני הכפורת' requires sprinkling right on the כפורת. But the בית שני had no כפורת, so no sprinkling could ever have been done there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected to רבי יהודה: Since you read 'אל' as exact, you must also read 'על' as exact. But then, in the בית שני, where there was no ארון and no כפורת, would you say the כהן גדול did not do the sprinklings at all?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רבי יהודה's method of reading the words exactly by showing it leads to an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said 'אל פני הכפורת' is exact. If so, the phrase 'על פני הכפורת' in the sprinkling פסוק (ויקרא 16:14) should also be exact and mean right on the כפורת. But in the בית שני there was no כפורת, and the sprinklings were still done, so reading the words exactly seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The Ark and its golden cover

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two words. 'אל' (toward) is what רבי יהודה already read as exact. The new challenge is about 'על' (on), which in the corrected wording replaces 'אל נכח'.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected to this, against Rabbi Yehuda:
Since 'el' (toward) is exact,
is 'al' (on) also exact?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets; read 'על' instead, from ויקרא 16:14.

phrases.english: But what about the Second Temple,
where there was no Ark and no Ark Cover?
Would you really say he did not perform the sprinklings?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יהודה's method of reading the words exactly, which was the basis of Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's rule that the wording of the פסוק is exact
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'על' is exact, sprinkling needs a real כפורת. The בית שני had none, yet sprinklings were done there. That would be impossible.

steps.title: The place set aside for the ארון is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא answers from the פסוק 'וכפר את מקדש הקדש': the sprinkling can be done at the place set aside for the ארון, even when the ארון itself is not there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: The פסוק says, 'And he shall atone for מקדש הקדש.' This means the place that is set aside for the holy ארון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא defends רבי יהודה by showing that a פסוק allows the sprinkling at the ארון's place when the ארון is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'מקדש הקדש' as 'the place made holy for the holy item', which means the spot where the ארון belongs. So even if 'על' is exact, the בית שני sprinklings were valid, because they were done on the ארון's place. רבי יהודה's exact reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy place of the holy item, read here as the ארון's place
The place set aside for the holy item

steps.whatToRemember: Even for רבי יהודה, the sprinklings in the בית שני were valid, because the place set aside for the ארון takes the place of the ארון.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא, אָמַר קְרָא:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said: The verse says:
'And he shall make atonement for the most holy place'
meaning the place that is set aside for the holy item.
phrases.notes: The 'holy item' is the ארון. Its spot still counts even when it's gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge from Step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without an ארון, sprinkling 'on' the כפורת would be impossible, so the exact reading would have to be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: A פסוק teaches that the place set aside for the ארון works in its place, so the exact reading can stand.

steps.title: רבא begins a new answer: both teachings follow רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a different way to settle the two ברייתות about the פרה אדומה sprinklings: both of them follow רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This teaching and that teaching both follow רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new answer. רבא begins by saying both clashing ברייתות agree with רבנן, and he will explain how in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer split the two ברייתות between רבי יהודה and רבנן. רבא rejects that split and says both follow רבנן. He still needs to show some other reason why one ברייתא calls the sprinkling valid and the other calls it not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both teachings
The red heifer, whose blood is sprinkled toward the entrance

phrases.english: Rava said:
This one and that one both follow the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: He means the two ברייתות that disagree about the פרה אדומה sprinkling that isn't aimed right at the entrance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב יוסף exchange and returns to the original clash between the ברייתות, offering a different answer from Steps 20-21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer: both sources follow one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clash between the ברייתות comes from a split between רבי יהודה and רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both ברייתות follow רבנן. The explanation continues in the next line.
